name: Korean citizenship by naturalisation

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 5 or more consecutive years of legal residence in Korea, a clean criminal record, financial self-sufficiency, and a passing score on the Korean-language and social/cultural knowledge exam (satisfied by KIIP completion).
requirements.fix_path: Accrue 5 consecutive years of legal residence while maintaining financial self-sufficiency and completing KIIP.

requirement_groups.name: Simplified naturalisation for F-6 marriage migrants

requirements.blocker_text: A foreign spouse of a Korean national who has maintained the marriage and resided in Korea for 2 or more years may apply for simplified naturalisation. An alternate route exists for spouses who married abroad and moved to Korea partway through the marriage: 3 years of marriage plus 1+ year of Korean residence.
requirements.fix_path: Maintain the marriage and Korean residence until the applicable threshold is met.

requirements.blocker_text: For individuals with outstanding, recognised talent or achievements deemed to benefit Korea's national interest in fields such as science, the economy, culture and arts, sports, or education -- granted by Ministry of Justice recommendation and Presidential approval, bypassing the standard 5-year residence requirement. There is no codified points threshold or guaranteed acceptance criterion; approval is discretionary.

outcome_override.physical_presence_requirement: no minimum prior residence period required at all

evidence_required.document: Proof of 5 years' continuous legal residence (general track) or 2-3 years on F-6 status (marriage track)
KIIP completion certificate or passing score on the naturalisation exam
Clean criminal record and proof of financial self-sufficiency

sources.title: HiKorea -- Korea Immigration Service's official portal for visa categories, ARC, and stay procedures

Easy-to-Find Practical Law (easylaw.go.kr, Ministry of Government Legislation) -- Immigrants by marriage: International Marriage, Status and Nationality, confirming the 2-year simplified-naturalisation track for F-6 holders

notes: Three genuinely distinct naturalisation mechanisms, correctly modeled as separate OR-logic groups: general naturalisation (5-year residence, no dual citizenship retained), simplified marriage naturalisation (2-3 years depending on where the marriage began, dual citizenship explicitly permitted as one of Korea's narrow exceptions to its single-nationality rule), and exceptional-talent naturalisation (fully discretionary, no minimum residence, dual citizenship also permitted). dual_citizenship_allowed varies genuinely by group -- true for the marriage and exceptional-talent tracks, false for the general track -- confirmed identically across easylaw.go.kr (a tier-1 Ministry of Government Legislation source) for the marriage exception and HiKorea for the general rule; this is a real structural difference between naturalisation mechanisms within the same country, the same kind of within-country variation documented for Saudi Arabia's discretionary-vs-administrative citizenship tracks elsewhere in this dataset. exceptional_talent's nat_talent requirement is modeled hard:false rather than hard:true because, like Saudi Arabia's Article 9 exceptional-merit track and the UAE's 2021 exceptional-merit decree, there is no codified, testable acceptance criterion -- approval is a discretionary Ministry of Justice recommendation followed by Presidential approval, not a scoreable test, so forcing a hard:true classification would misrepresent the mechanism as more rule-bound than it actually is. citizenship_after_months = 0 across all three groups correctly reflects that naturalisation IS citizenship, the same convention used throughout this dataset (pl_naturalisation, sa_naturalisation, sa_citizenship_by_descent's automatic-descent group) -- the real barrier is each group's residence/marriage/discretion prerequisite, not a further wait after grant.
